anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of De Oratione exists (only copyrighted Greer/O'Meara/Oulton-Chadwick); nothing to compare against. Sense checked against the Greek and cited Scripture wording.

apparatus: Jn 13:1,3; 14:23,28; 16:5 local sayings must be read worthily.
Phil 2:7 kenosis reversed into fullness; Jn 20:17 mind-ascent.
Challenge to literalists: show a nature besides the material.
Gen 3:8-9 reductio (audible footfalls, hiding that hides).
Lev 26:12/2 Cor 6:16 indwelling; Gen 4:16 Cain; Qoh 5:1; Isa 66:1.

choices.why: sunkatabasis = condescension-accommodation; the Word humbles to human worth so we may contemplate him perfected.
aporrhoē is Wis 7:25's own term for Wisdom; Origen closes the essence-withdrawal argument with it.

pass_a_gloss: 'In the heavens' cannot circumscribe God (smaller than heaven, body, divisible, corruptible): Johannine goings/comings prove local language must be read worthily; kenosis returns to fullness and guides ours; Jn 20:17 is mind-ascent. Gen 3:8-9 collapses literalism (footfalls, real hiding, 'Where art thou?'). God walks in saints as in Paradise; heaven is saints, Christ the Father's throne, the church his footstool; essence stays uncommunicated while effluence reaches creatures.
